decisions.quote:
Resembling the pattern seen in Experiment 1, Experiment
2b
failed to replicate the symmetrical interaction between face sex and expression on expression and sex categorization seen for the larger picture set used in Experiment
2a
. Rather, an asymmetrical interaction was found, in that poser sex affected the categorization of emotional expressions, whereas expression did not affect the categorization of faces by sex. This pattern deviates from that seen in Experiment
1b
, in which no interaction was observed in either sex or expression categorization, but is consistent with the pattern of results reported in studies that had employed the Garner paradigm (Atkinson et al.,
2005
; Karnadewi & Lipp,
2011
).
decisions.reason: The paper's stated design and intent is to test whether Aguado et al.'s (2009) symmetrical interaction is moderated by stimulus set size (32 vs. 4 faces). Atkinson et al. (2005) is cited alongside Le Gal and Bruce (2002) and Karnadewi and Lipp (2011) only to motivate the negative expectation that Aguado et al.'s symmetrical interaction would be absent with four faces; the paper does not re-test Atkinson et al.'s empirical findings (either their orthogonal-vs.-control Garner interference or their post-hoc 2x2 orthogonal-condition ANOVA, which yielded no interaction at all), and instead explicitly evaluates Experiments 1b and 2b as failures to replicate the large-set symmetrical interaction while noting post-hoc consistency in Experiment 2b.

Karnadewi and Lipp (2011) is not re-tested as a replication or reproduction target. Its contrast with Aguado et al. (2009) motivates manipulating set size within Aguado et al.'s paradigm to test whether the symmetrical interaction disappears at four faces, and both small-set experiments (1b and 2b) are explicitly framed and evaluated as failing to replicate Aguado et al.'s symmetrical interaction rather than testing Karnadewi and Lipp's asymmetrical Garner effect. The passing mention of a post-hoc 2x2 ANOVA on Karnadewi and Lipp's (2011) orthogonal condition in the Introduction is an incidental background check ruling out analytic differences, not a reproduction of Karnadewi and Lipp's reported Garner finding.

failed to replicate the pattern of results reported by Aguado et al. (
2009
), in that no interaction between poser sex and emotional expression was found if participants were presented repeatedly with a subset of the faces used by Aguado et al. and in Experiment
1a
. This evidence for independent processing of sex and emotion cues is consistent with the results reported by Le Gal and Bruce (
2002
).
decisions.reason: Le Gal and Bruce (2002) is not re-tested by this paper. The source never specifies Le Gal and Bruce's stimulus set or procedure, lumps it with Atkinson et al. (2005) and Karnadewi and Lipp (2011) despite their differing empirical results solely to motivate predicting the absence of Aguado et al.'s (2009) symmetrical interaction with four faces, and explicitly frames Experiment 1b as a failed replication of Aguado et al. (2009) whose null result is merely consistent with Le Gal and Bruce (2002).

Aggregating across the paper's four experiments testing Aguado et al.'s (2009) categorization paradigm, the large-set experiments (1a and 2a) replicated the original symmetrical interaction whereas the small-set experiments (1b and 2b) explicitly failed to replicate it, yielding a mixed outcome.
